pr.title: gh-148286: Fail on new UB in CI
pr.body:
Trying to debug a bit, it should be detecting https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/148166 (and also screaming about it), but it isn't. Mirroring what we do for the TSan job.

Just chucked everything in suppressions for now, they should be reviewed as it may have actual bugs.

               || ''
             }}.txt handle_segv=0" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
         else
-          echo "UBSAN_OPTIONS=${SAN_LOG_OPTION}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+          echo "UBSAN_OPTIONS=${SAN_LOG_OPTION} halt_on_error=1 suppressions=${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/Tools/ubsan/suppressions.txt" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
review_comments.body:
If a developer passes `./configure --with-undefined-behavior` locally, they'll possibly miss non-fatal issues during the build. Given configure already knows about UBSAN, we can just add `UBSAN_OPTIONS` into the Makefile when this option is passed. You then get consistent behaviour in CI and locally without having to explain this to people every time they can't reproduce a problem on their machine (because they missed it in the output).

Ditto the other sanitizer options like `--with-memory-sanitizer` and `--with-thread-sanitizer`. The weird "don't abort" behaviour for the sanitizer runtimes confuses everybody and if handling UBSAN, it would avoid some future pain to handle those two now, even if not run in CI.

i.e. I don't really see why this should be in CI specifically? Move it forward and then it'll naturally fail in CI because you're handling it whenever UBSAN is enabled.

issue_comments.body:
I've never been so happy to see the CI fail :-)

```
[3](https://github.com/python/cpython/actions/runs/24037637122/job/70101135069?pr=148168#step:11:144)
==> /home/runner/work/cpython/cpython/san_log.26255 <==
Modules/binascii.c:1243:42: runtime error: left shift of 129 by 24 places cannot be represented in type 'int'
SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior Modules/binascii.c:1243:42
```

We got there in the end: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/111758#issuecomment-1793789864 :)

I'd assumed that https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/135578 or https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/136820 included that but I didn't check.

LGTM, thank you!
Consider opening an issue, which we could use to track the fixes too.
